# Dashboards, panel by panel

<!-- Generated by stack/monitoring/scripts/dashboard-docs.mjs from stack/monitoring/grafana/dashboards — do not edit by hand. -->

Every panel of every dashboard: the question it answers, how it is drawn, the exact query, its unit and the colour
thresholds. Grafana is one rendering of these rows; the query column plus [signals.md](signals.md) is enough to rebuild a
panel on any provider (see [porting.md](porting.md)). Plain-language definitions of the KPIs behind the panels:
[kpis.md](kpis.md).

| dashboard | folder | panels | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Database & SQL](#cvhome-database-sql) | data | 13 | The database side of every service: the connection pool, how many statements each request costs, and how slow each statement family is. Built from Hikari meters and the JDBC client spans. |
| [Outbox & Events](#cvhome-outbox-events) | data | 8 | The transactional outbox that carries domain events between services: is it keeping up, is anything stuck or failed, how long does processing take. |
| [Auth](#cvhome-auth) | edge | 10 | Identity and access: the two authorization servers (uaa for staff, cua for shoppers), the gateway sign-in, and where 401/403 come from across the platform. |
| [Edge: spg & landing-ui](#cvhome-edge) | edge | 13 | The shopper-facing edge: the pod gateway (spg) per route and the storefront (landing-ui) page renders and their upstream calls. Built from the spans, since neither runs Micrometer. |
| [Load test vs app](#cvhome-load-test-vs-app) | load-testing | 19 | One k6 run (pick the testid) next to what the application did during it, on the same time axis: where the load went, where latency broke, which resource ran out first. |
| [Logs & Errors](#cvhome-logs-errors) | observability | 8 | What the services are saying: error volume per service, the most frequent error messages and exception classes, and a searchable log view where every line links to its trace. |
| [Traces](#cvhome-traces) | observability | 9 | Ready-made trace searches: the slowest requests, the failed ones, the failed service-to-service calls, the slow SQL. Each row opens the full trace, with its log lines one click away. |
| [Bottlenecks](#cvhome-bottlenecks) | platform | 12 | Where is the system saturating? Every resource that can run out — request threads, database connections, CPU, GC, executor queues, caches — as a share of its limit, next to traffic and latency, so the first one to hit its ceiling under load is obvious. |
| [JVM & Runtime](#cvhome-jvm-runtime) | platform | 12 | The Java runtime of each service: memory, garbage collection, threads, CPU, file handles. The place to look for leaks and undersized heaps during a soak. |
| [Platform Overview](#cvhome-platform-overview) | platform | 15 | Is the platform healthy right now? One page: are we inside our SLOs, which service is burning its error budget, and what is firing. |
| [Service RED](#cvhome-service-red) | platform | 18 | Rate, Errors, Duration for one service (or several): what it is asked, how often it fails and with which status, how slow it is per route. |
| [Service-to-Service](#cvhome-service-to-service) | platform | 9 | The calls between services: which edges exist, how often each fails, how slow it is from the caller's side. Built from the traces (service graph) and the HTTP client meters. |

## Database & SQL

<a id="cvhome-database-sql"></a>

- **uid** `cvhome-database-sql` · **file** `stack/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/data/cvhome-database-sql.json` · **default range** now-1h · **refresh** 10s
- **Purpose:** The database side of every service: the connection pool, how many statements each request costs, and how slow each statement family is. Built from Hikari meters and the JDBC client spans.
- **Variables:** `service` (Service: `label_values(http_server_requests_seconds_count, service_name)`)
- **Links to:** Bottlenecks, Traces

| panel | answers | type | query | unit | thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| *Connection pool* — **Pool: active / idle / pending / max** | Connections in use, spare, threads waiting, and the ceiling. Pending above zero is exhaustion. | time series | PromQL: `max by (service_name) (hikaricp_connections_active{service_name=~"$service"})`<br>PromQL: `max by (service_name) (hikaricp_connections_idle{service_name=~"$service"})`<br>PromQL: `max by (service_name) (hikaricp_connections_pending{service_name=~"$service"})`<br>PromQL: `max by (service_name) (hikaricp_connections_max{service_name=~"$service"})` | short | — |
| *Connection pool* — **Pool utilisation** | Connections in use as a share of the pool. | gauge | PromQL: `cvhome:hikari_pool:utilisation{service_name=~"$service"}` | percentunit | orange ≥ 0.6, red ≥ 0.8 |
| *Connection pool* — **Connection timeouts** | Requests that gave up waiting for a connection in the selected range. Must be zero. | single value | PromQL: `sum(increase(hikaricp_connections_timeout_total{service_name=~"$service"}[$__range]))` | short | orange ≥ 1, red ≥ 5 |
| *Connection pool* — **Time to get a connection (p95)** | How long a request waits for a pooled connection. Rises before pending does. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:hikari_acquire:p95_5m` | s | orange ≥ 0.01, red ≥ 0.1 |
| *Connection pool* — **Time a connection is held (p95)** | How long each borrowed connection is kept. Long holds with short statements mean long transactions or work done while holding a connection. | time series | PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (service_name, le) (rate(hikaricp_connections_usage_seconds_bucket{service_name=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))` | s | orange ≥ 0.1, red ≥ 1 |
| *Statements* — **Statements / s by operation and table** | Database traffic per service, split by operation and table. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (db_operation, db_sql_table) (cvhome:sql:rate5m{service_name=~"$service"})` | ops | — |
| *Statements* — **Statement p95 by family** | Slow tail per statement family ("SELECT catalog.product"). Target: under 100 ms. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:sql:p95_5m{service_name=~"$service"}` | s | orange ≥ 0.1, red ≥ 0.5 |
| *Statements* — **Statement latency distribution** | Where statements land in time. | heatmap | PromQL: `sum by (le) (rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_seconds_bucket{service_name=~"$service",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_CLIENT",db_system="postgresql"}[$__rate_interval]))` | — | — |
| *Statements* — **Statements per request** | Average number of statements each incoming request costs. Above 10 is almost always an N+1 loop. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:sql_per_request:ratio5m{service_name=~"$service"}` | short | orange ≥ 5, red ≥ 10 |
| *Statements* — **Top statements** | Statement families by rate, with their p95 and error rate. Click a name to see the traces behind it. | table | PromQL: `topk(20, sum by (service_name, span_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"$service",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_CLIENT",db_system="postgresql"}[5m])))`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:sql:p95_5m{service_name=~"$service"}`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:sql_errors:rate5m{service_name=~"$service"}` | — | — |
| *Statements* — **N+1 suspects** | Requests that ran more than 20 statements in one trace. | table | TraceQL: `{resource.service.name=~"$service" && span.db.system="postgresql"} \| count() > 20` | — | — |
| *Statements* — **Schema changes at runtime** | DDL statements (CREATE/ALTER) after start-up. schema.sql runs at boot; anything later is ddl-auto: update doing what the DDL file should. | table | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, span_name) (increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"$service",db_operation=~"CREATE\|ALTER\|DROP"}[$__range])) > 0` | — | — |
| *Statements* — **JDBC connections (DataSource view)** | The same pool seen through the JDBC meters; a mismatch with the Hikari view is a second DataSource. | time series | PromQL: `max by (service_name) (jdbc_connections_active{service_name=~"$service"})`<br>PromQL: `max by (service_name) (jdbc_connections_max{service_name=~"$service"})` | short | — |

## Outbox & Events

<a id="cvhome-outbox-events"></a>

- **uid** `cvhome-outbox-events` · **file** `stack/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/data/cvhome-outbox-events.json` · **default range** now-1h · **refresh** 10s
- **Purpose:** The transactional outbox that carries domain events between services: is it keeping up, is anything stuck or failed, how long does processing take.
- **Variables:** `service` (Service: `label_values(http_server_requests_seconds_count, service_name)`)
- **Links to:** Database & SQL

| panel | answers | type | query | unit | thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Outbox records by status** | Records waiting, processing, done and failed per service (present once the outbox meter ships). A growing NEW count is a consumer falling behind. | time series | PromQL: `max by (service_name, status) (cvhome_outbox_records{service_name=~"$service"})` | short | — |
| **Oldest pending record** | Age of the oldest record still waiting. The lag a downstream service sees. | time series | PromQL: `max by (service_name) (cvhome_outbox_oldest_pending_seconds{service_name=~"$service"})` | s | orange ≥ 60, red ≥ 300 |
| **Outbox polling / s** | How often each service touches its outbox tables (the poller reads outbox_partition/outbox_instance every 2 s, and each shipped record is an UPDATE). Zero means the scheduler is not running. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"$service",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_CLIENT",db_sql_table=~"outbox_.*"}[$__rate_interval]))` | ops | — |
| **Outbox statement p95** | Slow tail of the outbox table statements; a poll slower than its 2 s interval is the backlog growing. | time series | PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (service_name, le) (rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_seconds_bucket{service_name=~"$service",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_CLIENT",db_sql_table=~"outbox_.*"}[$__rate_interval])))` | s | orange ≥ 0.5, red ≥ 2 |
| **Outbox statement errors / s** | Outbox table statements that failed. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, span_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"$service",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_CLIENT",db_sql_table=~"outbox_.*",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[$__rate_interval]))` | ops | orange ≥ 0.01, red ≥ 0.1 |
| **Outbox table statements / s** | Database traffic on the outbox tables. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, db_operation) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"$service",db_sql_table=~".*outbox.*"}[$__rate_interval]))` | ops | — |
| **Failed background work** | Scheduled and internal work (outbox handlers, partition rebalance, expiry and recovery jobs) that failed, latest first. | table | TraceQL: `{resource.service.name=~"$service" && span:kind=internal && status=error}` | — | — |
| **Outbox log lines** | Everything the services log about the outbox, warnings and errors first. | log view | LogQL: `{service_name=~"$service"} \|~ "(?i)outbox" \| detected_level=~"error\|warn"` | — | — |

## Auth

<a id="cvhome-auth"></a>

- **uid** `cvhome-auth` · **file** `stack/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/edge/cvhome-auth.json` · **default range** now-1h · **refresh** 10s
- **Purpose:** Identity and access: the two authorization servers (uaa for staff, cua for shoppers), the gateway sign-in, and where 401/403 come from across the platform.
- **Links to:** Service RED, Logs & Errors

| panel | answers | type | query | unit | thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| *Rejections* — **401 / 403 by service** | Auth rejections per service. 401 = no valid token, 403 = valid token without the permission. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:http_server_auth_rejections:rate5m` | reqps | — |
| *Rejections* — **Bare 401s (no route)** | 401s decided by the JWT filter before routing: they carry no body and no route. A burst here is an expired or wrong-issuer token in a client. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{status="401",uri="UNKNOWN"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *Rejections* — **Rejections by reason** | Where each rejection was decided and why (present once the cvhome_auth_rejections meter ships). | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, status, reason, source) (rate(cvhome_auth_rejections_total[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *Rejections* — **429 rate limited** | The login rate limiter and public-POST limiter engaging. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{status="429"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *Authorization servers* — **Token / authorize / login requests / s** | Traffic on the OAuth2 endpoints of uaa and cua. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, uri, status) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"uaa\|cua",uri=~"/oauth2/.*\|/login.*\|/api/v1/public/registration"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *Authorization servers* — **Token endpoint p95** | How long issuing a token takes. Login SLO 2.5 s end to end. | time series | PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (service_name, uri, le) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{service_name=~"uaa\|cua",uri=~"/oauth2/token\|/oauth2/authorize\|/login.*"}[$__rate_interval])))` | s | orange ≥ 1, red ≥ 2.5 |
| *Authorization servers* — **JWKS fetches by clients** | Resource servers fetching signing keys. A steady stream instead of a trickle means key caching is broken. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, server_address) (rate(http_client_request_duration_seconds_count{server_address=~"uaa.*\|cua.*\|.*gateway.com"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *Gateway* — **Gateway sign-in and session** | Seller sign-in traffic through store-core-gateway, and its in-memory session count (present once the session gauge ships). | time series | PromQL: `sum by (uri, status) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name="store-core-gateway",uri=~"/login.*\|/oauth2/.*"}[$__rate_interval]))`<br>PromQL: `max(cvhome_gateway_sessions)` | reqps | — |
| *Gateway* — **Billing guard (402) and relay failures at the gateway** | Requests the gateway refused for a lapsed subscription (402) or could not relay (5xx). | time series | PromQL: `sum by (status) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name="store-core-gateway",status=~"402\|5.."}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *Gateway* — **Authentication failures (log)** | Failed sign-ins and token problems as logged by uaa, cua and the gateway. | log view | LogQL: `{service_name=~"uaa\|cua\|store-core-gateway"} \|~ "(?i)authentication failed\|bad credentials\|invalid_grant\|invalid_token\|access denied\|rate.?limit"` | — | — |

## Edge: spg & landing-ui

<a id="cvhome-edge"></a>

- **uid** `cvhome-edge` · **file** `stack/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/edge/cvhome-edge.json` · **default range** now-1h · **refresh** 10s
- **Purpose:** The shopper-facing edge: the pod gateway (spg) per route and the storefront (landing-ui) page renders and their upstream calls. Built from the spans, since neither runs Micrometer.
- **Links to:** Overview, Load test vs app

| panel | answers | type | query | unit | thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| *spg (pod gateway)* — **spg requests / s by route** | Traffic through the pod gateway per routed service. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (span_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="spg",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *spg (pod gateway)* — **spg p95 by route** | Slow tail per routed service as the gateway sees it (includes the upstream). | time series | PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (span_name, le) (rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_seconds_bucket{service_name="spg",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"}[$__rate_interval])))` | s | orange ≥ 0.5, red ≥ 2 |
| *spg (pod gateway)* — **spg responses / s by status** | Status codes the gateway returned. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (http_response_status_code) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="spg",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *spg (pod gateway)* — **spg errors / s by route** | Gateway spans that ended in error, per route. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (span_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="spg",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *landing-ui (storefront)* — **Page renders / s** | Server-side renders per page pattern. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (span_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="landing-ui",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *landing-ui (storefront)* — **Page render p95** | Slow tail of a server-side render, per page pattern. Storefront page SLO 3 s (dev server locally). | time series | PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (span_name, le) (rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_seconds_bucket{service_name="landing-ui",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"}[$__rate_interval])))` | s | orange ≥ 1, red ≥ 3 |
| *landing-ui (storefront)* — **Upstream fetch p95 by call** | How long the storefront waits for each backend call it makes while rendering. | time series | PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (span_name, le) (rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_seconds_bucket{service_name="landing-ui",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_CLIENT",span_name=~"fetch .*"}[$__rate_interval])))` | s | orange ≥ 0.5, red ≥ 2 |
| *landing-ui (storefront)* — **Upstream fetch errors / s** | Backend calls from the storefront that failed. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (span_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="landing-ui",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_CLIENT",span_name=~"fetch .*",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *landing-ui (storefront)* — **Distinct span names (landing-ui)** | Cardinality guard: how many different span names the storefront emits. Above 200 means URLs are leaking into names again. | single value | PromQL: `count(count by (span_name) (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="landing-ui"}))` | short | orange ≥ 100, red ≥ 200 |
| *Browser (k6 web vitals, last run)* — **LCP p75** | Largest Contentful Paint as measured by k6 browser runs. Target under 4 s locally. | single value | PromQL: `max(max_over_time(k6_browser_web_vital_lcp_p75[$__range]))` | s | orange ≥ 2.5, red ≥ 4 |
| *Browser (k6 web vitals, last run)* — **CLS p75** | Cumulative Layout Shift. Target under 0.1. | single value | PromQL: `max(max_over_time(k6_browser_web_vital_cls_p75[$__range]))` | short | orange ≥ 0.1, red ≥ 0.25 |
| *Browser (k6 web vitals, last run)* — **INP p75** | Interaction to Next Paint. Target under 200 ms. | single value | PromQL: `max(max_over_time(k6_browser_web_vital_inp_p75[$__range]))` | s | orange ≥ 0.2, red ≥ 0.5 |
| *Browser (k6 web vitals, last run)* — **TTFB p75** | Time To First Byte. Target under 1.5 s locally. | single value | PromQL: `max(max_over_time(k6_browser_web_vital_ttfb_p75[$__range]))` | s | orange ≥ 0.8, red ≥ 1.5 |

## Load test vs app

<a id="cvhome-load-test-vs-app"></a>

- **uid** `cvhome-load-test-vs-app` · **file** `stack/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/load-testing/cvhome-load-test-vs-app.json` · **default range** now-3h · **refresh** 30s
- **Purpose:** One k6 run (pick the testid) next to what the application did during it, on the same time axis: where the load went, where latency broke, which resource ran out first.
- **Variables:** `testid` (Test run: `label_values(k6_http_reqs_total, testid)`) · `name` (Endpoint: `label_values(k6_http_reqs_total{testid="$testid"}, name)`) · `service` (Service: `label_values(http_server_requests_seconds_count, service_name)`)
- **Links to:** Bottlenecks, Service RED, Database & SQL

| panel | answers | type | query | unit | thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| *The run* — **Peak VUs** | Highest number of virtual users in the run. | single value | PromQL: `max(max_over_time(k6_vus{testid="$testid"}[$__range]))` | short | — |
| *The run* — **Requests** | Requests k6 sent. | single value | PromQL: `sum(increase(k6_http_reqs_total{testid="$testid"}[$__range]))` | short | — |
| *The run* — **Failed share** | Share of requests k6 counted as failed (unexpected status), from the request counters over the whole run. SLO: under 1 %. | single value | PromQL: `(sum(max_over_time(k6_http_reqs_total{testid="$testid",expected_response="false"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / sum(max_over_time(k6_http_reqs_total{testid="$testid"}[$__range]))` | percentunit | orange ≥ 0.01, red ≥ 0.05 |
| *The run* — **Dropped iterations** | Iterations an open-model scenario could not start because every VU was busy: the load generator, not the app, hit its limit. | single value | PromQL: `sum(max_over_time(k6_dropped_iterations_total{testid="$testid"}[$__range])) or vector(0)` | short | orange ≥ 1, red ≥ 10 |
| *The run* — **Orders placed** | Orders the run created. | single value | PromQL: `max(max_over_time(k6_orders_placed_total{testid="$testid"}[$__range])) or vector(0)` | short | — |
| *The run* — **Journey errors** | Share of user journeys that failed at any step (average of k6's per-flush rate over the run). | single value | PromQL: `avg(avg_over_time(k6_journey_errors_rate{testid="$testid"}[$__range]))` | percentunit | orange ≥ 0.02, red ≥ 0.05 |
| *Load and latency, k6 side* — **VUs and requests / s (k6)** | The load shape: virtual users and the request rate they achieved. Rate flattening while VUs climb is the system saturating. | time series | PromQL: `max(k6_vus{testid="$testid"})`<br>PromQL: `sum(rate(k6_http_reqs_total{testid="$testid"}[30s]))` | reqps | — |
| *Load and latency, k6 side* — **k6 p95 by endpoint** | Latency as the user saw it per endpoint name. Thresholds per name live in load-testing/k6/config/thresholds.js (product 0.5 s, search 0.8 s, checkout 2 s, pages 3 s). | time series | PromQL: `max by (name) (k6_http_req_duration_p95{testid="$testid",expected_response="true",name=~"$name"})` | s | orange ≥ 0.5, red ≥ 2 |
| *Load and latency, k6 side* — **k6 failures / s by endpoint and status** | Requests with an unexpected status. 429 = the limiter, 402 = the billing guard, 5xx = the platform. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (name, status) (rate(k6_http_reqs_total{testid="$testid",expected_response="false"}[30s]))` | reqps | — |
| *Load and latency, k6 side* — **Journeys p95** | End-to-end time of each user journey (home, product, purchase, …). | time series | PromQL: `max by (journey) (k6_journey_duration_ms_p95{testid="$testid"})` | s | orange ≥ 3, red ≥ 5 |
| *What the application did* — **App requests / s by service** | Server-side traffic per service during the run. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[30s]))` | reqps | — |
| *What the application did* — **App p95 by service** | Server-side latency per service (30 s windows). | time series | PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (service_name, le) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{service_name=~"$service",uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[30s])))` | s | orange ≥ 0.5, red ≥ 2 |
| *What the application did* — **App 5xx / s by service** | Server errors during the run. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",status=~"5.."}[30s]))` | reqps | — |
| *What the application did* — **Service-to-service failure share** | Edges that started failing under load. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:s2s_failed:ratio_rate5m` | percentunit | orange ≥ 0.005, red ≥ 0.05 |
| *What ran out* — **Saturation: threads, pool, cpu, gc** | Every limit as a share, on one axis. The first line to reach 0.8 is the bottleneck of this run. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:tomcat_threads:utilisation`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:hikari_pool:utilisation`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:jvm_cpu:ratio`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:jvm_gc_pause:ratio5m` | percentunit | orange ≥ 0.6, red ≥ 0.8 |
| *What ran out* — **Waiting for a database connection** | Threads blocked on the pool. Above zero the pool is the bottleneck. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:hikari_pending:max` | short | orange ≥ 1, red ≥ 3 |
| *What ran out* — **Statements per request and SQL p99** | Query cost per request, and the slow tail of SQL, during the run. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:sql_per_request:ratio5m`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:sql:p99_5m` | short | — |
| *What ran out* — **Heap after GC** | Live heap share during a soak: a rising floor is a leak. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:jvm_heap_after_gc:ratio` | percentunit | orange ≥ 0.7, red ≥ 0.85 |
| *What ran out* — **Application errors during the run** | Error lines from the selected services while the run was going. | log view | LogQL: `{service_name=~"$service"} \| detected_level="error"` | — | — |

## Logs & Errors

<a id="cvhome-logs-errors"></a>

- **uid** `cvhome-logs-errors` · **file** `stack/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/observability/cvhome-logs-errors.json` · **default range** now-1h · **refresh** 10s
- **Purpose:** What the services are saying: error volume per service, the most frequent error messages and exception classes, and a searchable log view where every line links to its trace.
- **Variables:** `lsvc` (Service: `label_values({service_name=~".+"}, service_name)`) · `level` (Level) · `search` (Contains)
- **Links to:** Traces, Service RED

| panel | answers | type | query | unit | thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Log lines / s by level** | Volume per level. A jump in error or warn is the first sign of trouble even before a metric moves. | time series | LogQL: `sum by (detected_level) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$lsvc"} \| detected_level=~"$level" [$__auto]))` | short | — |
| **Error lines / s by service** | Which service is producing the errors. | time series | LogQL: `sum by (service_name) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$lsvc"} \| detected_level="error" [$__auto]))` | short | — |
| **Top error messages** | The most frequent error messages (first 80 characters) in the selected range. | table | LogQL: `topk(20, sum by (service_name, msg) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$lsvc"} \| detected_level="error" \| regexp "^(?P<msg>.{0,80})" [$__range])))` | — | — |
| **Exception classes** | Exception class names found in error and warning lines, most frequent first. | table | LogQL: `topk(20, sum by (service_name, ex) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$lsvc"} \| detected_level=~"error\|warn" \| regexp "(?P<ex>[A-Za-z0-9_.$]+(Exception\|Error))" [$__range])))` | — | — |
| **Error codes returned to callers** | The error codes the @ControllerAdvice logged ("CATALOG.PRODUCT.NOT_FOUND [traceId=…]"), most frequent first. | table | LogQL: `topk(20, sum by (service_name, code) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$lsvc"} \|~ "\\[traceId=" \| regexp "^(?P<code>[0-9]{3} [A-Z_]+\|[A-Z][A-Z_.]+) \\[traceId=" [$__range])))` | — | — |
| **Remote and provider failures** | Calls to a peer service (RemoteServiceException) or a third party (ExternalProviderException) that failed. | table | LogQL: `sum by (service_name, ex) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$lsvc"} \| regexp "(?P<ex>RemoteServiceException\|ExternalProviderException\|[A-Za-z]+ApiUnavailableException)" [$__range]))` | — | — |
| **Observation scope-leak warnings** | Count of the "Observation … is not the same as the one set as this scope's parent" warning. It must be zero; it was firing on every scheduled refresh of the gateway before the fix. | single value | LogQL: `sum(count_over_time({service_name=~".+"} \|= "ObservationThreadLocalAccessor" [$__range]))` | short | orange ≥ 1, red ≥ 10 |
| **Logs** | The log view. Filter by service, level and free text; expand a line and click "View trace" to open its trace in Tempo. | log view | LogQL: `{service_name=~"$lsvc"} \| detected_level=~"$level" \|~ "$search"` | — | — |

## Traces

<a id="cvhome-traces"></a>

- **uid** `cvhome-traces` · **file** `stack/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/observability/cvhome-traces.json` · **default range** now-1h · **refresh** 10s
- **Purpose:** Ready-made trace searches: the slowest requests, the failed ones, the failed service-to-service calls, the slow SQL. Each row opens the full trace, with its log lines one click away.
- **Variables:** `tsvc` (Service: `label_values(traces_span_metrics_calls_total, service_name)`)
- **Links to:** Logs & Errors, Service-to-Service

| panel | answers | type | query | unit | thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Slow requests (> 500 ms)** | Server spans slower than the storefront SLO, slowest first. | table | TraceQL: `{resource.service.name=~"$tsvc" && span:kind=server && duration > 500ms}` | — | — |
| **Failed requests** | Server spans that ended in error. | table | TraceQL: `{resource.service.name=~"$tsvc" && span:kind=server && status=error}` | — | — |
| **5xx responses** | Requests answered with a server error. | table | TraceQL: `{resource.service.name=~"$tsvc" && span:kind=server && span.http.response.status_code >= 500}` | — | — |
| **403 and 404 responses** | Requests refused for permission or an unknown resource. | table | TraceQL: `{resource.service.name=~"$tsvc" && span:kind=server && (span.http.response.status_code = 403 \|\| span.http.response.status_code = 404)}` | — | — |
| **Failed service-to-service calls** | Client spans (one service calling another) that failed, with the destination. | table | TraceQL: `{resource.service.name=~"$tsvc" && span:kind=client && status=error && span.db.system = nil}` | — | — |
| **Slow SQL (> 100 ms)** | Individual statements slower than 100 ms. | table | TraceQL: `{resource.service.name=~"$tsvc" && span.db.system="postgresql" && duration > 100ms}` | — | — |
| **Statement-heavy requests** | Traces with more than 20 statements: N+1 candidates. | table | TraceQL: `{resource.service.name=~"$tsvc" && span.db.system="postgresql"} \| count() > 20` | — | — |
| **Failed background work** | Scheduled and internal work (outbox handlers, jobs) that failed. | table | TraceQL: `{resource.service.name=~"$tsvc" && span:kind=internal && status=error}` | — | — |
| **Busiest server spans** | Span names by rate with their error share, from the span metrics. Click a name to search its traces. | table | PromQL: `topk(25, sum by (service_name, span_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"$tsvc",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"}[5m])))`<br>PromQL: `sum by (service_name, span_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"$tsvc",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by (service_name, span_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"$tsvc",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"}[5m]))` | — | — |

## Bottlenecks

<a id="cvhome-bottlenecks"></a>

- **uid** `cvhome-bottlenecks` · **file** `stack/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/platform/cvhome-bottlenecks.json` · **default range** now-1h · **refresh** 10s
- **Purpose:** Where is the system saturating? Every resource that can run out — request threads, database connections, CPU, GC, executor queues, caches — as a share of its limit, next to traffic and latency, so the first one to hit its ceiling under load is obvious.
- **Variables:** `service` (Service: `label_values(http_server_requests_seconds_count, service_name)`)
- **Links to:** Overview, Database & SQL, JVM & Runtime, Load test vs app

| panel | answers | type | query | unit | thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| *Saturation matrix* — **Saturation by service** | Each resource as a share of its limit, per service. Red is the bottleneck. | table | PromQL: `cvhome:tomcat_threads:utilisation`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:hikari_pool:utilisation`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:hikari_pending:max`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:jvm_cpu:ratio`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:jvm_gc_pause:ratio5m`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:jvm_heap_after_gc:ratio`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:sql_per_request:ratio5m` | — | — |
| *The knee* — **Traffic vs p95** | Request rate (left axis) against p95 latency (right axis). The point where the rate flattens while p95 climbs is the capacity of the system as configured. | time series | PromQL: `sum(rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[$__rate_interval]))`<br>PromQL: `max(cvhome:span_server:p95_5m{service_name=~"$service"})`<br>PromQL: `max(k6_vus)` | reqps | — |
| *Request threads (Tomcat)* — **Request threads busy / max** | Threads serving requests against the configured maximum. At the max, new requests queue in the connector. | time series | PromQL: `max by (service_name) (tomcat_threads_busy{service_name=~"$service"})`<br>PromQL: `max by (service_name) (tomcat_threads_config_max{service_name=~"$service"})` | short | — |
| *Request threads (Tomcat)* — **Request thread utilisation** | Busy share of the request thread pool. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:tomcat_threads:utilisation` | percentunit | orange ≥ 0.6, red ≥ 0.8 |
| *Request threads (Tomcat)* — **Connections** | Open connections on the HTTP connector against its maximum. | time series | PromQL: `max by (service_name) (tomcat_connections_current{service_name=~"$service"})`<br>PromQL: `max by (service_name) (tomcat_connections_config_max{service_name=~"$service"})` | short | — |
| *Request threads (Tomcat)* — **Executor pools** | Async and scheduler executors: active threads and queued tasks. A growing queue is work arriving faster than it is done. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, name) (executor_active_threads{service_name=~"$service"})`<br>PromQL: `sum by (service_name, name) (executor_queued_tasks{service_name=~"$service"})` | short | — |
| *Database pool* — **Waiting for a connection** | Threads blocked waiting for a pooled connection. Any value above zero means the pool is the bottleneck. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:hikari_pending:max` | short | orange ≥ 1, red ≥ 3 |
| *Database pool* — **Pool utilisation** | Connections in use as a share of the pool (5 per service locally, 10 on Fargate). | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:hikari_pool:utilisation` | percentunit | orange ≥ 0.6, red ≥ 0.8 |
| *Caches* — **Cache hit ratio** | Share of cache reads served from the cache, per cache (present once recordStats is on). | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, cache) (rate(cache_gets_total{service_name=~"$service",result="hit"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (service_name, cache) (rate(cache_gets_total{service_name=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval]))` | percentunit | — |
| *Caches* — **Cache size and evictions** | Entries held and evictions per second. Evictions with a low hit ratio mean the cache is too small. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, cache) (cache_size{service_name=~"$service"})`<br>PromQL: `sum by (service_name, cache) (rate(cache_evictions_total{service_name=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval]))` | short | — |
| *Telemetry pipeline* — **Collector exporter** | Spans and metrics the collector received vs exported. A gap is the collector dropping data (memory limiter). | time series | PromQL: `sum by (exporter) (rate(otlp_exporter_seen_total[$__rate_interval]))`<br>PromQL: `sum by (exporter) (rate(otlp_exporter_exported_total[$__rate_interval]))` | ops | — |
| *Telemetry pipeline* — **Collector scrape** | Whether Prometheus can reach the collector's metrics endpoint (1 = yes). | single value | PromQL: `up{job="otel-collector"}` | short | orange ≥ 0, red ≥ 1 |

## JVM & Runtime

<a id="cvhome-jvm-runtime"></a>

- **uid** `cvhome-jvm-runtime` · **file** `stack/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/platform/cvhome-jvm-runtime.json` · **default range** now-1h · **refresh** 10s
- **Purpose:** The Java runtime of each service: memory, garbage collection, threads, CPU, file handles. The place to look for leaks and undersized heaps during a soak.
- **Variables:** `service` (Service: `label_values(http_server_requests_seconds_count, service_name)`)
- **Links to:** Bottlenecks, Service RED

| panel | answers | type | query | unit | thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Heap used by pool** | Live heap per memory pool. A sawtooth is healthy; a floor that keeps rising across GCs is a leak. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, jvm_memory_pool_name) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{service_name=~"$service",jvm_memory_type="heap"})` | bytes | — |
| **Heap after GC vs limit** | Live data after the last collection as a share of the maximum heap. Above 85 % the JVM spends its time collecting instead of serving. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:jvm_heap_after_gc:ratio` | percentunit | orange ≥ 0.7, red ≥ 0.85 |
| **Non-heap used** | Metaspace, code cache and compressed class space. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, jvm_memory_pool_name) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{service_name=~"$service",jvm_memory_type="non_heap"})` | bytes | — |
| **GC pause share** | Share of wall-clock time the JVM was paused for garbage collection. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:jvm_gc_pause:ratio5m` | percentunit | orange ≥ 0.02, red ≥ 0.05 |
| **GC pause p95** | Slow tail of individual GC pauses, per collector. | time series | PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (service_name, jvm_gc_name, le) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_bucket{service_name=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])))` | s | orange ≥ 0.1, red ≥ 0.5 |
| **GC collections / s** | How often each collector runs. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, jvm_gc_name, jvm_gc_action) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval]))` | ops | — |
| **Threads** | Live JVM threads. Steadily climbing = a pool that is never bounded. | time series | PromQL: `max by (service_name) (jvm_thread_count{service_name=~"$service"})` | short | — |
| **CPU** | CPU used by each JVM process, and the whole machine. | time series | PromQL: `max by (service_name) (jvm_cpu_recent_utilization_ratio{service_name=~"$service"})`<br>PromQL: `max(system_cpu_usage)` | percentunit | orange ≥ 0.6, red ≥ 0.8 |
| **Load average (1m)** | Runnable threads on the machine; above the CPU count means queueing. | time series | PromQL: `max(system_load_average_1m)`<br>PromQL: `max(system_cpu_count)` | short | — |
| **Open file descriptors** | Sockets and files held open, against the limit. Climbing towards the limit means connections are not being closed. | time series | PromQL: `max by (service_name) (process_files_open{service_name=~"$service"})`<br>PromQL: `max by (service_name) (process_files_max{service_name=~"$service"})` | short | — |
| **Loaded classes** | Classes loaded in the JVM; growth after start-up hints at class-generation leaks (proxies, scripts). | time series | PromQL: `max by (service_name) (jvm_class_count{service_name=~"$service"})` | short | — |
| **Uptime** | Time since the JVM started. A reset is a restart. | single value | PromQL: `max by (service_name) (process_uptime_seconds{service_name=~"$service"})` | s | — |

## Platform Overview

<a id="cvhome-platform-overview"></a>

- **uid** `cvhome-platform-overview` · **file** `stack/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/platform/cvhome-platform-overview.json` · **default range** now-1h · **refresh** 10s
- **Purpose:** Is the platform healthy right now? One page: are we inside our SLOs, which service is burning its error budget, and what is firing.
- **Links to:** Service RED, Bottlenecks, Service-to-Service, Database & SQL, Logs & Errors

| panel | answers | type | query | unit | thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| *Service level* — **Availability (1h)** | Share of requests answered without a 5xx over the last hour, all services together. SLO 99.9 %. | single value | PromQL: `1 - (sum(rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{status=~"5..",uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[1h])) or vector(0)) / sum(rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[1h]))` | percentunit | orange ≥ 0.999, red ≥ 0.995 |
| *Service level* — **Storefront latency SLO** | Share of storefront reads (catalog, content, merchant, inventory GETs) answered under 500 ms. SLO 95 %. | single value | PromQL: `min(cvhome:slo_latency_storefront:good_ratio_rate5m)` | percentunit | — |
| *Service level* — **Checkout latency SLO** | Share of checkout and payment writes answered under 2 s. SLO 95 %. | single value | PromQL: `min(cvhome:slo_latency_checkout:good_ratio_rate5m)` | percentunit | — |
| *Service level* — **Services reporting** | How many services sent metrics in the last 2 minutes. 12 Java services are expected. | single value | PromQL: `count(count by (service_name) (process_uptime_seconds))` | short | — |
| *Service level* — **Firing alerts** | Number of alert rules currently firing (see the table at the bottom). | single value | PromQL: `count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing"}) or vector(0)` | short | orange ≥ 1, red ≥ 3 |
| *Service level* — **Requests / s** | Total request rate across all services, health probes excluded. | single value | PromQL: `sum(rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *Error budget* — **Availability burn rate (1h and 6h windows)** | How fast each service is spending its 5xx error budget. 1 = exactly on budget; above 14.4 for an hour means the month's budget is gone in two days. | time series | PromQL: `max by (service_name) (cvhome:slo_availability:burn_rate1h)`<br>PromQL: `max by (service_name) (cvhome:slo_availability:burn_rate6h)` | short | orange ≥ 6, red ≥ 14.4 |
| *Error budget* — **Storefront latency burn rate** | Same idea for the latency SLO: how fast the "5 % may be slower than 500 ms" budget is spent. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:slo_latency_storefront:burn_rate1h` | short | orange ≥ 6, red ≥ 14.4 |
| *Traffic and errors* — **Requests / s by service** | Traffic per service. A drop to zero on one service while the others keep going is a dead service. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *Traffic and errors* — **Responses / s by status class** | What the platform is answering: 2xx good, 4xx the caller's problem (or auth), 5xx ours. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (status) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{status=~"5..",uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[$__rate_interval]))`<br>PromQL: `sum by (status) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{status=~"4..",uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *Traffic and errors* — **p95 latency by service (server spans)** | The slowest 5 % of requests per service, including spg and landing-ui. Compare against the SLO lines of the storefront (0.5 s) and checkout (2 s). | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:span_server:p95_5m` | s | orange ≥ 0.5, red ≥ 2 |
| *Traffic and errors* — **5xx ratio by service** | Share of each service's requests that failed on our side. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:http_server_errors:ratio_rate5m` | percentunit | orange ≥ 0.001, red ≥ 0.01 |
| *Per service* — **Service table** | Every service on one line: traffic, failure share, latency, pool and CPU. Click a service name for its RED dashboard. | table | PromQL: `sum by (service_name) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[5m]))`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:http_server_errors:ratio_rate5m`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:span_server:p95_5m`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:hikari_pool:utilisation`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:tomcat_threads:utilisation`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:jvm_cpu:ratio`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:jvm_heap_after_gc:ratio` | — | — |
| *Per service* — **Service map** | Who calls whom, from the traces: every edge is a service-to-service or database call with its rate and failure count. | node graph | Tempo: `serviceMap (Tempo → traces_service_graph_* in Prometheus)` | — | — |
| *Alerts* — **Firing alerts** | Alert rules in the firing state, with their labels. Meaning and first steps: docs/alerts.md. | table | PromQL: `ALERTS{alertstate="firing"}` | — | — |

## Service RED

<a id="cvhome-service-red"></a>

- **uid** `cvhome-service-red` · **file** `stack/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/platform/cvhome-service-red.json` · **default range** now-1h · **refresh** 10s
- **Purpose:** Rate, Errors, Duration for one service (or several): what it is asked, how often it fails and with which status, how slow it is per route.
- **Variables:** `service` (Service: `label_values(http_server_requests_seconds_count, service_name)`) · `uri` (Route: `label_values(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service"}, uri)`)
- **Links to:** Overview, Database & SQL, JVM & Runtime, Bottlenecks

| panel | answers | type | query | unit | thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| *Rate* — **Requests / s by route** | Traffic per route of the selected service. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (method, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri",uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *Rate* — **Responses / s by status** | Every status code the service answered with. A new colour appearing is a new failure mode. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (status) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *Errors by status (selected time range)* — **400 Bad Request** | Requests the service rejected as malformed or invalid (validation errors). Coming from our own frontends this is a bug in the caller. | single value | PromQL: `sum(increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri",status="400"}[$__range])) or vector(0)` | short | orange ≥ 50, red ≥ 200 |
| *Errors by status (selected time range)* — **401 Unauthorized** | Requests with no or an invalid token. A bare 401 from the JWT filter carries no body and no route (uri="UNKNOWN"). | single value | PromQL: `sum(increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri",status="401"}[$__range])) or vector(0)` | short | orange ≥ 50, red ≥ 200 |
| *Errors by status (selected time range)* — **403 Forbidden** | Authenticated callers that lack the permission. A silent spike usually means a permission token with no case in CustomPermissionEvaluator. | single value | PromQL: `sum(increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri",status="403"}[$__range])) or vector(0)` | short | orange ≥ 50, red ≥ 200 |
| *Errors by status (selected time range)* — **404 Not Found** | Unknown resource or route. | single value | PromQL: `sum(increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri",status="404"}[$__range])) or vector(0)` | short | orange ≥ 50, red ≥ 200 |
| *Errors by status (selected time range)* — **409 Conflict** | Optimistic-locking and uniqueness conflicts (duplicate SKU, stale layout version). | single value | PromQL: `sum(increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri",status="409"}[$__range])) or vector(0)` | short | orange ≥ 50, red ≥ 200 |
| *Errors by status (selected time range)* — **422 Unprocessable** | Business-rule refusals, including provider rejections re-emitted as ours and plan-limit hits. | single value | PromQL: `sum(increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri",status="422"}[$__range])) or vector(0)` | short | orange ≥ 50, red ≥ 200 |
| *Errors by status (selected time range)* — **429 Too Many** | The rate limiter engaging (uaa/cua login and public POSTs). | single value | PromQL: `sum(increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri",status="429"}[$__range])) or vector(0)` | short | orange ≥ 50, red ≥ 200 |
| *Errors by status (selected time range)* — **5xx Server error** | Failures on our side. Every one of these counts against the availability SLO. | single value | PromQL: `sum(increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri",status=~"5.."}[$__range])) or vector(0)` | short | orange ≥ 1, red ≥ 10 |
| *Errors by status (selected time range)* — **Failed routes** | Which route fails with which status and exception, most frequent first. Click a row to open matching traces. | table | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, method, uri, status, exception) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri",status=~"4..\|5.."}[$__range])) > 0` | — | — |
| *Duration* — **Latency p50 / p95 / p99** | How slow requests are for most callers (p50), for the slow tail (p95) and for the worst (p99). Storefront SLO 0.5 s, checkout 2 s. | time series | PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri",uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[$__rate_interval])))`<br>PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri",uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[$__rate_interval])))`<br>PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri",uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[$__rate_interval])))` | s | orange ≥ 0.5, red ≥ 2 |
| *Duration* — **Latency distribution** | Where requests land in time: a band moving up is everything getting slower; a second band appearing is one route or one dependency getting slow. | heatmap | PromQL: `sum by (le) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri",uri!~"/actuator.*\|UNKNOWN\|root"}[$__rate_interval]))` | — | — |
| *Duration* — **Slowest routes (p95)** | Routes ordered by their p95 over the last 5 minutes. | table | PromQL: `topk(15, cvhome:http_server_requests:p95_5m{service_name=~"$service",uri=~"$uri"})` | — | — |
| *Why* — **Exceptions / s by class** | Which exception classes the service is throwing to its callers. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (exception) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service_name=~"$service",exception!="none"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *Why* — **Server spans in error / s by name** | The same failures seen from the traces, per span name; useful for non-HTTP work (scheduled tasks, outbox handlers). | time series | PromQL: `sum by (span_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"$service",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *Why* — **Auth rejections / s** | 401 and 403 by reason, counted where they are decided (the JWT filter or the permission evaluator) — present once the cvhome_auth_rejections meter ships. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (status, reason) (rate(cvhome_auth_rejections_total{service_name=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| *Why* — **Error and warning logs** | The service's own error and warning lines for the time range; each line links to its trace. | log view | LogQL: `{service_name=~"$service"} \| detected_level=~"error\|warn"` | — | — |

## Service-to-Service

<a id="cvhome-service-to-service"></a>

- **uid** `cvhome-service-to-service` · **file** `stack/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/platform/cvhome-service-to-service.json` · **default range** now-1h · **refresh** 10s
- **Purpose:** The calls between services: which edges exist, how often each fails, how slow it is from the caller's side. Built from the traces (service graph) and the HTTP client meters.
- **Links to:** Overview, Traces

| panel | answers | type | query | unit | thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Service map** | Every caller → callee edge seen in the traces. Node colour follows the failure share; edge labels show rate and failures. | node graph | Tempo: `serviceMap (Tempo → traces_service_graph_* in Prometheus)` | — | — |
| **Edges** | One row per caller → callee edge with its call rate, failure share and p95 as the caller sees it. | table | PromQL: `cvhome:s2s:rate5m`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:s2s_failed:ratio_rate5m`<br>PromQL: `cvhome:s2s:p95_5m` | — | — |
| **Failure share by edge** | Share of calls on each edge that failed. Anything above 0.5 % sustained is a broken dependency. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:s2s_failed:ratio_rate5m` | percentunit | orange ≥ 0.005, red ≥ 0.05 |
| **p95 by edge (caller side)** | How long the caller waits for each callee, slow tail. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:s2s:p95_5m` | s | orange ≥ 0.5, red ≥ 2 |
| **Calls / s by edge** | Traffic on each edge. | time series | PromQL: `cvhome:s2s:rate5m` | reqps | — |
| **Outgoing HTTP errors by destination** | From the caller's HTTP client: responses that came back 4xx/5xx, by destination host and status. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, server_address, http_response_status_code) (rate(http_client_request_duration_seconds_count{http_response_status_code=~"4..\|5.."}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| **Outgoing transport failures** | Calls that got no HTTP answer at all (connection refused, timeout), by exception type. These are the RemoteServiceException 502s. | table | PromQL: `sum by (service_name, server_address, error_type) (increase(http_client_request_duration_seconds_count{error_type!=""}[$__range])) > 0` | — | — |
| **Database edges: calls / s** | Each service's traffic to the database as the service graph sees it. | time series | PromQL: `sum by (client) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{connection_type="database"}[$__rate_interval]))` | reqps | — |
| **Unknown peers** | Edges to or from something that sent no spans (a browser, k6, or a host without instrumentation). Useful to spot an uninstrumented dependency. | table | PromQL: `sum by (client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{connection_type="virtual_node"}[5m]))` | — | — |
